## Quick answers
**Is BillZino's invoice generator free?** Yes — creating and downloading PDFs is free and unlimited, with no signup and no watermark.

**Do I need an account?** No. The invoice is built in the browser and downloaded as a PDF.

**Can I get a Word or Excel invoice?** No — BillZino outputs PDF. See the guide on building your own in Word, Excel or Google Docs.

**Does BillZino support e-invoicing (Factur-X, XRechnung)?** No. It produces ordinary PDF invoices. Check local e-invoicing rules with an accountant or tax authority.

**Does BillZino take payments?** No. Clients pay the user directly using the bank details or payment instructions on the invoice.

**What currencies are supported?** 50+, including USD, EUR, GBP and MAD.

**Which languages?** English, French, German and Spanish, including the labels on the exported PDF.

**What does an invoice need?** The word "Invoice", a unique number, issue and due dates, the seller's and buyer's details, itemised lines with quantity and price, subtotal, tax/discount, total due and payment instructions. Country-specific fields (tax IDs, mandatory legal mentions) are additional — see https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html.

## Formulas used by BillZino's calculators
- **VAT:** VAT = net × rate ÷ 100; gross = net × (1 + rate ÷ 100); net = gross ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100). Example at 20%: 1,000 net → 1,200 gross.
- **Markup:** markup % = (price − cost) ÷ cost × 100. Example: cost 100, price 150 → 50% markup.
- **Profit margin:** margin % = (price − cost) ÷ price × 100. Example: cost 100, price 150 → 33.3% margin.
- **Hourly rate:** (income wanted + business expenses) ÷ (billable hours per week × working weeks per year).
- **Late payment interest:** amount × annual rate ÷ 100 × days late ÷ 365, plus any fixed fee allowed by the contract.
- **Discount:** final price = price × (1 − discount ÷ 100); amount saved = price × discount ÷ 100.
- **Due date:** invoice date + number of days of the payment term (Net 30 = 30 days after the invoice date).

## Glossary of invoicing terms
- **Invoice** — a document a seller sends to a buyer to request payment for goods or services; it lists what was supplied, the amounts and the payment terms.
- **Tax invoice** — an invoice that shows the tax (VAT, GST or sales tax) separately. Many jurisdictions require specific fields for tax-registered sellers; the details vary by country.
- **Proforma invoice** — a preliminary invoice sent before goods or services are delivered, announcing the expected amount. It is not normally the final demand for payment.
- **Quote** — a price offer made before the work, usually valid for a set period. **Estimate** — an approximate price that may change as the scope becomes clear.
- **Receipt** — a document confirming that payment has been received.
- **Credit note** — a document issued by the seller that reduces or cancels the amount of an earlier invoice (for example after a return or a pricing error).
- **Purchase order (PO)** — a document from the buyer authorising a purchase; the seller's invoice should reference the PO number.
- **Net 30 (Net 15, Net 45, Net 60)** — payment is due that many days after the invoice date. **2/10 Net 30** — a 2% discount if paid within 10 days, otherwise the full amount is due within 30 days.
- **Line item** — one row of an invoice: a description, a quantity and a rate, giving an amount.
- **Subtotal** — the sum of all line items before tax, discount and shipping.
- **Due date** — the date by which payment must be received.
- **Invoice number** — a unique, usually sequential identifier (for example INV-0042 or 2026-001) that makes every invoice easy to find and avoids duplicates.
- **VAT / GST / sales tax** — consumption taxes. VAT and GST are charged at each stage of the supply chain and the rate depends on the country; US sales tax is charged at the point of sale and varies by state and by what is sold.
- **Markup** — the percentage added to cost to reach the price: (price − cost) ÷ cost. **Margin** — the share of the price that is profit: (price − cost) ÷ price.
- **Late payment fee / interest** — a charge on an overdue invoice, usually a percentage per year or a fixed fee allowed by the contract or by law.
- **Retainer / deposit** — an advance payment before or during the work, credited against later invoices.

## How to create an invoice with BillZino (3 steps)
Source: https://billzino.com/

1. **Add your details** — your business, your client and your line items.
2. **Make it yours** — pick a colour, add your logo, sign it or stamp it, and set tax, discount and currency.
3. **Send it** — download the PDF and send it to your client by email.

## The 8 parts of an invoice
Source: https://billzino.com/#guide

1. **Title & invoice number** — Label the document “Invoice” and give it a unique, sequential number like INV-0042.
2. **Issue & due date** — Say when it was issued and exactly when payment is due — a real date, not “soon”.
3. **Your details** — Business name, address, email and your tax ID if you have one.
4. **Client details** — Who you are billing, their address and a contact for questions.
5. **Line items** — Description, quantity, rate and amount for every product or hour.
6. **Subtotal, discount & tax** — Shown separately so the maths is easy to follow — and easy to check.
7. **Total amount due** — The final figure in the right currency, impossible to miss.
8. **How to pay** — Bank details or a payment link, plus your terms such as Net 30.

## Three mistakes that delay payment
Get paid faster

#### Three mistakes that delay payment

-
**No clear due date**

Without an exact date there is no deadline, so clients pay when they get round to it.[Set payment terms →](https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)
-
**Missing or duplicate numbers**

Sequential numbers keep your records clean and make every invoice easy to find.[Number invoices properly →](https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)
-
**Payment details buried**

Put bank details or the payment link where the client cannot miss them.[See a full example →](https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)
## Frequently asked questions (home page)
Source: https://billzino.com/

**Q: Is the BillZino invoice generator really free?**

Yes. Creating, customising and downloading invoices, quotes, tax invoices and receipts as PDF is free, with no signup and no watermark.

**Q: Do I need to sign up to create an invoice?**

No — you can build and download an invoice as a PDF right now with no account.

**Q: Is there a watermark on the PDF?**

No. One click downloads a clean, print-ready A4 PDF with only your invoice on it — no BillZino watermark and no forced branding.

**Q: What should an invoice include?**

An invoice should include the word “Invoice”, a unique invoice number, the issue and due dates, your details, your client’s details, an itemised list with quantity and price, the subtotal, any tax or discount, the total due, and how to pay you. See our guide: how to write an invoice.

**Q: What is the difference between an invoice, a receipt and a quote?**

A quote offers a price before the work, an invoice asks the customer to pay, and a receipt confirms that payment was received. BillZino creates all of them — see invoice vs receipt vs quote.

**Q: Can I use my own logo, brand colors, signature and stamp?**

Yes. Upload your logo straight onto the invoice and drag to resize it, pick an accent color that carries through the whole document, draw your signature on the built-in pad, and add a stamp image you can place anywhere on the page.

**Q: Can I add tax, discounts, or shipping?**

Yes, each is a simple toggle in the builder — turn one on, set the percentage or amount, and it's factored into the total automatically.

**Q: Does BillZino process payments for me?**

No — BillZino creates and tracks invoices, it doesn't move money. You add your own bank details or payment instructions, and your client pays you directly.

**Q: How do I know when a client has paid?**

That's currently set up by request while we onboard new accounts personally — contact us to get set up.

**Q: Can I create an invoice online for free without an account?**

Yes. BillZino is a free invoice creator: open the builder on this page, add your details and line items, and download the PDF. No account, no signup and no watermark, and everything stays in your browser until you download or send the invoice.

**Q: What is the difference between an invoice maker, an invoice creator and an invoice generator?**

Nothing important: they are different names for the same tool, software that turns your details and line items into a finished invoice. BillZino works as all three. You fill in the fields, it calculates the totals and tax, and you download a PDF.

**Q: How do I make an invoice with my logo?**

Upload your logo in the builder, pick a template colour, then add your business details and line items. The logo, signature and stamp appear on the A4 PDF. You can also start from a free invoice template for your trade.

**Q: Can I make an invoice on my phone?**

Yes. The builder works on phones and tablets: tap any field to edit, add line items, switch the currency and download the PDF. There is no app to install.

**Q: What format does a tax invoice follow?**

The usual tax invoice format shows seller and buyer details, a unique invoice number, the date, each line with quantity and price, the tax rate and amount, and the total. The generator lays these out for you; a sales tax invoice follows the same structure.

An estimate is approximate and can change; a quote is a fixed price, usually valid for a stated period.

Usually no, unless your terms say otherwise. It is an indication of price, not a contract.

State clearly whether the amount includes tax. Many estimates show the total excluding tax and add a note.

30 days is common. Put the validity date on the document so there is no ambiguity later.

Yes. Reuse the same line items, update the amounts to the final figures, and reference the estimate number.

(Source: https://billzino.com/estimate-generator.html)

**Q: Is a proforma invoice a real invoice?**

No. It is an advance notice of the amount. The real invoice is issued after delivery and is the document used for accounting and tax.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: Do I charge VAT on a proforma invoice?**

Usually no tax is due at the proforma stage. The real invoice carries the tax. Confirm with your accountant for cross-border cases.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: Can a proforma invoice be used for customs?**

Yes, many customs authorities accept a proforma for valuation before shipment, but the commercial invoice is required for the final clearance.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: What is the difference between a proforma and a quote?**

A quote offers a price before the client commits. A proforma confirms the exact amount for a sale that is already agreed.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: Do I need to number proforma invoices?**

Yes, use a separate sequence such as PF-0001 so they are never confused with real invoices.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: What is a proforma invoice?**

A proforma invoice is a preliminary document that lists what you will sell, the quantities and the prices before the sale is final. It is not a request for payment in the accounting sense, and it does not replace the final invoice. Some countries also call it a pro forma invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

**Q: What is the difference between a proforma invoice and a commercial invoice?**

A proforma invoice is issued before shipment as an estimate of the sale; a commercial invoice is issued after the sale and is the final record used for payment and customs. BillZino does not generate customs documents.

(Source: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html)

### Calculators

**Q: How do I calculate VAT on a price?**

Multiply the net price by the rate and divide by 100. At 20%, a 1,000 service carries 200 VAT and a 1,200 total.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I remove VAT from a total?**

Divide the gross amount by 1 + (rate ÷ 100). At 20%, 1,200 ÷ 1.2 = 1,000 net.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: Is VAT the same as sales tax?**

No. VAT is collected at each stage of the supply chain; sales tax is usually collected once at the final sale. The maths for a single invoice is similar.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: Do I charge VAT to clients abroad?**

Often not, or at a zero rate, depending on the rules for exports and reverse charges. Confirm with your accountant.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: Does BillZino calculate VAT automatically?**

Yes. Turn on tax in the builder, enter the rate, and the total updates as you type.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I work out VAT inclusive and exclusive prices?**

VAT = net × rate ÷ 100. Gross (VAT inclusive) = net × (1 + rate ÷ 100). Net = gross ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100). The calculator applies this VAT formula both ways.

(Source: https://billzino.com/vat-calculator.html)

**Q: How is a late payment fee calculated?**

It is usually simple interest: invoice amount × annual rate ÷ 100 × days late ÷ 365, plus any fixed fee your contract allows.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: Can I charge a late fee without a contract?**

It depends on the law where you operate. Many countries allow statutory interest on business debts, but a written clause in your terms is the safest route.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a typical late payment interest rate?**

For business-to-business debts, 8% above the central bank rate is common in the EU and the UK. In the US, check your state limit.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: Should I charge a late fee on the tax part of the invoice?**

Usually yes, because the tax is part of the amount owed. Confirm with your accountant for your jurisdiction.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I add the fee to the invoice?**

Create a new line item called Late payment fee, enter the calculated amount, and mention the period it covers.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate interest on an overdue invoice?**

Multiply the invoice amount by the annual interest rate, divide by 365 and multiply by the number of days late. The calculator does this for you, and works as a late fee calculator for a flat fee too.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-fee-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate a Net 30 due date?**

Add 30 calendar days to the invoice date. An invoice dated 1 March is due 31 March.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: Does the due date count the invoice day?**

Usually no. Day zero is the invoice date and counting starts the next day.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: What does Net 30 EOM mean?**

Payment is due 30 days after the end of the invoice month. An invoice dated 12 March is due 30 April.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: Are weekends included in Net 30?**

Yes, unless the contract says business days. Calendar days include weekends and holidays.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: What happens if the due date falls on a weekend?**

Some contracts move it to the next business day; others do not. The invoice should state the rule.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate a due date?**

Add the payment terms to the invoice date: net 30 means 30 days after it. The calculator does this and shows the exact date.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-due-date-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a 50% markup on 100?**

A selling price of 150: 50 profit on a 100 cost.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: Is markup the same as margin?**

No. Markup is based on cost; margin is based on the selling price. A 50% markup equals a 33.3% margin.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I get a 40% margin?**

Divide the cost by (1 − 0.40). A 100 cost needs a price of 166.67.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a good markup for a service business?**

Service businesses usually price from an hourly rate; the equivalent markup is often 2–3× the direct cost of delivering the hour.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: Does markup include tax?**

No. Calculate markup on the net price, then add tax on the invoice separately.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate markup percentage?**

Markup percentage = (selling price − cost) ÷ cost × 100. For example, a product that costs 80 and sells for 100 has a 25% markup. This markup formula is what the calculator applies.

(Source: https://billzino.com/markup-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a good profit margin?**

It depends on the industry. Retail often runs 5–10%, services 20–50%, software much higher. Compare with your own sector, not with a generic number.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate margin from cost and price?**

(price − cost) ÷ price × 100. A 100 price with a 60 cost is a 40% margin.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: What is the difference between gross and net margin?**

Gross margin counts only direct costs; net margin also subtracts overheads, salaries and tax.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: Can margin be negative?**

Yes, when the price is below the cost. That is a loss on every sale.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I increase margin without raising prices?**

Reduce the direct cost, bundle a higher-margin item, or remove a discount.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: What is the profit margin formula?**

Profit margin % = (revenue − cost) ÷ revenue × 100. A product sold for 100 that costs 80 has a 20% margin. Markup vs margin: markup is measured against cost, margin against the selling price.

(Source: https://billzino.com/margin-calculator.html)

**Q: How many billable hours should I assume?**

20–30 per week for most freelancers. If you are starting out and have no pipeline, assume fewer.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: Should the hourly rate include tax?**

No. Calculate the rate before tax, then add tax on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a day rate?**

Usually 6–8 billable hours at the hourly rate. Many freelancers charge 8 hours for a day even if the client uses fewer.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I raise my rate?**

Raise it for new clients first, then for existing ones at renewal. Give notice in writing.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: Does this calculator work for agencies?**

It works for any time-based business, but agencies should add overhead per person and a utilisation target.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate a freelance hourly rate?**

Hourly rate formula: (target yearly income + yearly expenses) ÷ billable hours. Count only the hours you can actually bill, since admin and unpaid time do not earn income.

(Source: https://billzino.com/hourly-rate-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate a 15% discount?**

Multiply the price by 0.15 to get the saving, then subtract it. On 500, the saving is 75 and the final price is 425.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: Should I discount before or after tax?**

Discount the net price, then calculate tax on the discounted amount.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: What is a 2/10 net 30 discount?**

2% off if the invoice is paid within 10 days instead of 30.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: Does a discount reduce VAT?**

Yes, tax is calculated on the discounted net amount.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I show a discount on an invoice?**

Add a discount line with the percentage or amount, then show the new subtotal and tax.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: How do I calculate a discount?**

Sale price = original price × (1 − discount ÷ 100). A 20% discount on 50 gives 40. The calculator works as a sale price calculator and shows the percentage off and the amount saved.

(Source: https://billzino.com/discount-calculator.html)

**Q: Are the Excel formulas on this page correct?**

Yes: Amount is =B8*C8, Subtotal is =SUM(D8:D17), tax is the subtotal times your rate and the total is subtotal plus tax. Adjust the row numbers and tax rate to your sheet.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-word-excel-google-docs.html)

**Q: How do I write a rent receipt?**

State the date, the landlord and tenant names, the property address, the period the rent covers, the amount and how it was paid, then sign or add the landlord’s name. The template above has a field for each.

(Source: https://billzino.com/rent-receipt-template.html)

**Q: Is a rent receipt legally required?**

It depends on where you live. Some places require one for cash payments or on request. Check your local rules or ask a local housing advice service; BillZino does not provide legal advice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/rent-receipt-template.html)

**Q: Can a landlord write a rent receipt by hand?**

Yes, a handwritten receipt with the same details is valid as a record. A typed PDF is easier to store, search and send.

(Source: https://billzino.com/rent-receipt-template.html)

**Q: How do I write a receipt for rent?**

Write the landlord’s and tenant’s names, the property address, the amount paid, the rental period, the date and the payment method, then sign it. A rent payment receipt gives both sides a record of the payment.

(Source: https://billzino.com/rent-receipt-template.html)

Write the date, who paid, who received, the amount, what it was for and add a signature. The template covers each field.

No. An invoice asks for payment; a receipt confirms that payment was made.

Shop and customer details, vehicle information, parts and labor listed separately, any diagnostic or shop fees, totals and payment terms.

Yes, it is clearer for the customer and for your own records.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-auto-repair.html)

**Q: What should a freelancer invoice include?**

Your details, the client's details, an invoice number, the date, a description of the work with hours or units, the amount, tax if applicable, the total and the payment terms.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-freelancer.html)

**Q: Should freelancers charge VAT?**

Only if you are registered for VAT or the local equivalent, or if the law requires it for your activity. Check your country's threshold.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-freelancer.html)

**Q: Can I invoice without a company?**

In most countries yes, as a sole trader or individual. You may still need a tax number. Confirm locally.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-freelancer.html)

**Q: How do I ask for a deposit?**

Send a deposit invoice before work starts, usually 30–50%, and reference it on the final invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-freelancer.html)

**Q: Is a freelance invoice legally required to be a PDF?**

No, but PDF is the standard because it cannot be edited accidentally and looks the same on every device.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-freelancer.html)

**Q: How should designers price a logo?**

Fixed price for a defined scope (concepts and revision rounds), with an hourly rate for anything beyond it.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-designer.html)

**Q: Should I hand over source files?**

Only if the contract says so. Many designers charge a handover fee or include it in the project price.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-designer.html)

**Q: How do I bill for revisions?**

Include two rounds in the project price, then bill extra rounds hourly with the hours shown on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-designer.html)

**Q: Do I charge tax on design work?**

Depends on your registration and country. Add the tax line separately on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-designer.html)

**Q: Can I invoice for stock images?**

Yes, as a separate line with the licence cost. Do not absorb it into the design fee.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-designer.html)

**Q: Should developers bill hourly or per project?**

Fixed price for a well-defined scope; hourly for maintenance, unclear scope or ongoing work.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-developer.html)

**Q: How do I invoice a milestone?**

Describe the milestone, reference the agreement, and invoice the agreed amount when the definition of done is met.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-developer.html)

**Q: Do I bill for meetings?**

Yes, if they are part of the work. Track them and show the hours on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-developer.html)

**Q: Can I pass through hosting costs?**

Yes, as a separate line. Do not hide them inside the development fee.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-developer.html)

**Q: What if the client delays feedback?**

Your contract should state that timelines shift accordingly. Invoice completed milestones regardless.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-developer.html)

**Q: How do consultants set a day rate?**

From the annual income target divided by realistic billable days (typically 180–220 per year), plus expenses.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-consultant.html)

**Q: Should I charge for travel time?**

Decide in advance and put it in the contract. Many consultants charge 50% of the day rate for travel.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-consultant.html)

**Q: Can I invoice a retainer monthly?**

Yes. State the period, what is included and the hours included before extra billing.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-consultant.html)

**Q: Do I need to show hours on a day-rate invoice?**

No, but showing the dates and the deliverable makes approval easier.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-consultant.html)

**Q: How do I handle taxes on consulting?**

Depends on registration and country. Add the tax line separately and confirm with your accountant.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-consultant.html)

**Q: What should a photographer's invoice include?**

Session fee, editing, travel, equipment, licensing and physical products, each as a separate line, plus your details, the client's details, the invoice number, the date and payment terms.

It depends on your registration and country. Many photographers charge VAT or sales tax once registered; check the threshold.

**Q: How do I invoice for image licensing?**

Add a line describing the media, territory and duration, with a price. Extended or commercial use should be a separate line.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-photographer.html)

**Q: Can I ask for a deposit?**

Yes. A booking fee of 30–50% is common and should be stated on the quote and the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-photographer.html)

**Q: Do I need a contract as well as an invoice?**

Yes. The invoice bills the work; the contract defines scope, copyright and cancellation. They serve different purposes.

Shoot days, editing, revisions, equipment, licensing, tax and payment terms.

Include a set number of rounds, then bill extra rounds hourly.

You do, unless the contract transfers it. State the licence granted on the invoice.

**Q: Can I charge for equipment?**

Yes, as a separate line or built into the day rate, but show it.

**Q: How do I handle a deposit?**

A 30–50% booking fee is common and should be deducted from the final invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-videographer.html)

**Q: How do architects invoice?**

By stage, by hourly rate or as a percentage of construction cost, depending on the appointment.

**Q: What are reimbursables?**

Costs you pay on the client's behalf, such as printing, travel and planning fees.

**Q: How do I bill for additional work?**

As a variation with a separate line and a reference to the instruction.

Yes, it ties payment to a deliverable and improves cash flow.

Monthly, listing the session dates, the rate per session, materials and any cancellation fees.

Yes, if your policy says so and the client agreed to it before booking.

Build it into the session rate rather than a separate line.

Per student, with the group size and the rate per student shown.

**Q: What should a contractor invoice include?**

The project and phase, labour hours and rate, materials with quantities, any equipment or permits, retainage if applicable, tax and the total due.

As separate lines with item, quantity and unit cost, usually with receipts attached for larger purchases.

**Q: What is retainage on a contractor invoice?**

A percentage held back by the client until the job is complete, commonly 5–10%.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-contractor.html)

**Q: Can I invoice for a deposit before starting?**

Yes, if the contract allows it. State what the deposit covers and how it is deducted from the final invoice.

**Q: Do I need to charge tax on labour?**

Depends on your jurisdiction. Some tax labour, some only materials. Confirm with your accountant.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-contractor.html)

**Q: What should a plumber invoice include?**

Call-out, labour hours, parts, the work performed, tax and payment terms.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-plumber.html)

**Q: Should I charge a call-out fee?**

Yes, if it is standard in your area. It covers travel and diagnosis and should be a separate line.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-plumber.html)

**Q: How do I invoice emergency work?**

Use an emergency rate and say so on the invoice, with the date and time of the call.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-plumber.html)

**Q: Can I bill parts at cost plus a markup?**

Yes, if the markup is agreed or standard in your trade. Show the part and the price.

**Q: Do I need to provide a warranty?**

State any workmanship warranty on the invoice so the client knows what is covered.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-plumber.html)

**Q: What should an electrician invoice include?**

Labour, materials, testing or certification, the work performed, tax and payment terms.

**Q: Should testing be a separate line?**

Yes. Testing and certification are distinct services with their own time and paperwork.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-electrician.html)

**Q: How do I bill for small extra works?**

As a separate line or a variation, agreed before the work starts.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-electrician.html)

**Q: Do I need to list materials?**

Yes, at least the main items. It protects you if the client questions the total.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-electrician.html)

**Q: How do I handle warranty callbacks?**

State the warranty period on the invoice and whether callbacks are free within it.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-electrician.html)

**Q: What should a cleaning invoice include?**

The date and duration of the clean, what was included, supplies, the rate, tax and payment terms.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-cleaner.html)

**Q: Should cleaners charge hourly or per job?**

Hourly for regular clients, per job for deep cleans with a written scope.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-cleaner.html)

**Q: How do I bill for supplies?**

As a separate line with the cost, or include a fixed consumables fee in the rate.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-cleaner.html)

**Q: Can I charge for travel?**

Yes, if it is agreed in advance. Add it as a separate line so the client sees it.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-cleaner.html)

**Q: Do cleaners need to charge tax?**

Depends on your registration and country. Add the tax line separately if you are registered.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-cleaner.html)

Labour, plants, materials, machinery, waste removal, tax and payment terms.

State the guarantee period and conditions on the invoice.

**Q: How do I bill maintenance?**

Monthly or per visit, with the tasks included.

Yes, as a separate line. It is a real cost and clients accept it when it is visible.

Take a deposit for materials and deduct it from the final invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-landscaper.html)

**Q: What should a catering invoice include?**

Menu and guest count, price per head, staff, equipment, deposit paid and the balance due.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-caterer.html)

**Q: How do I handle the deposit?**

Invoice it separately to reserve the date, then deduct it from the final invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-caterer.html)

**Q: What if fewer guests attend?**

Bill the guaranteed count stated in the contract, not the actual attendance.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-caterer.html)

**Q: Should staff be a separate line?**

Yes, with the number of staff and hours.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-caterer.html)

**Q: Do I charge tax on catering?**

Depends on the country and the food service rules. Check with your accountant.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-template-caterer.html)

### Guides

**Q: What is the minimum information an invoice needs?**

An invoice number, the date, your details, the client's details, a description and price of what you are charging for, and the total due.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: How do I number my invoices?**

Use a unique sequential number such as INV-0001, INV-0002. Do not reuse numbers.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: What does Net 30 mean on an invoice?**

Net 30 means the full payment is due 30 days after the invoice date.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Can I make an invoice for free?**

Yes. BillZino's invoice generator is free, needs no signup and adds no watermark to the PDF.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Is an invoice the same as a receipt?**

No. An invoice asks for payment; a receipt confirms payment was received.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: How do I make an invoice from scratch?**

To make an invoice: add your business details, add the client, give the invoice a number and date, list each item with quantity and price, add tax if needed, state the payment terms, then download the PDF. The builder lets you create an invoice in a couple of minutes.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: How do I fill out an invoice for services?**

Describe each service clearly, add the hours or quantity and your rate, show the subtotal, tax and total, and write the due date. An invoice for services is filled out the same way whatever your trade.

(Source: https://billzino.com/how-to-write-an-invoice.html)

**Q: What are the 12 things an invoice must include?**

Document type, invoice number, issue date, due date or terms, your legal name and address, your tax number if required, the client's name and address, the client's tax number for B2B, line items, tax and total, payment instructions, and notes such as a PO or reference.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Is an invoice number legally required?**

In most countries yes, or at least strongly expected. It must be unique and sequential.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Do I need to show tax separately?**

Yes for VAT and most sales-tax systems. Show the rate, the tax amount and the total.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: What is an ICE number on a Moroccan invoice?**

The Identifiant Commun de l'Entreprise, a shared business identifier used on invoices and official documents in Morocco.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Can I put a PO number on the invoice?**

Yes, and you should when the client provides one. It helps their accounts payable team match the payment.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: What are the basic invoice requirements?**

The basic required information on an invoice is: your details, the client’s details, a unique invoice number, the date, a description of goods or services with quantities and prices, the total, and payment terms. Local tax rules may add more invoice details.

(Source: https://billzino.com/what-to-include-on-an-invoice.html)

**Q: Do invoices need a number?**

In most countries yes, and it must be unique and sequential.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: Can I restart numbering each year?**

Yes, if the year is part of the number, for example 2026/001.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: What if I skip a number?**

Keep a note explaining why. A gap without explanation looks like a missing invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: Should quotes and invoices share a sequence?**

No. Use separate series so the documents cannot be confused.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: Can I renumber invoices after a mistake?**

No. Once issued, the number stays. Correct the content with a credit note.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: What invoice number format should I use?**

Use a sequential invoice numbering system, for example 2026-001, 2026-002, or INV-0001. A sequential format with no gaps or duplicates is easiest to audit; keep the same invoice number format for every client.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-numbering.html)

**Q: What does Net 30 mean?**

Payment is due 30 days after the invoice date.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: Does Net 30 include weekends?**

Yes, unless the contract specifies business days.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: What is Net 30 EOM?**

Payment is due 30 days after the end of the invoice month.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: What is 2/10 Net 30?**

A 2% discount if the invoice is paid within 10 days instead of 30.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: Can I charge a late fee after Net 30?**

Yes, if your terms or the law allow it. State the rate on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: What does due upon receipt mean?**

Due upon receipt means the client should pay as soon as they receive the invoice, with no grace period. Net 30 gives them 30 days instead.

(Source: https://billzino.com/net-30-payment-terms.html)

**Q: What is the difference between an invoice and a receipt?**

An invoice asks the customer to pay. A receipt confirms the customer has already paid.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html)

**Q: What is the difference between a quote and an invoice?**

A quote is an offer made before the work. An invoice is a request for payment sent after or at delivery.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html)

**Q: Is an estimate the same as a quote?**

No. A quote is a fixed price. An estimate is approximate and can change.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html)

**Q: Do I need all three documents?**

Not always. Many small businesses use only an invoice, and add a quote for larger jobs and a receipt when a customer needs proof of payment.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html)

**Q: Can I make these documents for free?**

Yes. BillZino's generators for invoices, quotes, tax invoices and receipts are free, with no signup and no watermark.

(Source: https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html)

**Q: Is a credit note the same as an invoice?**

No. An invoice requests payment; a credit note reduces an amount already invoiced.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: Do I need to issue a credit note for a refund?**

Yes, in most accounting systems the credit note is the document that reverses the sale, and the refund is the payment.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: Should a credit note show tax?**

Yes, if the original invoice included tax. The credit note must reverse the same rate.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: Can I just delete the invoice instead?**

No. Once an invoice has been sent it should stay in the sequence. Issue a credit note and reference it.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: Does BillZino create credit notes?**

You can create a document titled Credit Note in the builder and list the negative amounts; the PDF is generated the same way.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: What is a credit memo?**

A credit memo is another name for a credit note: a document that reduces what a client owes, for a return, a pricing error or a discount. Use a credit note template that refers to the original invoice number.

(Source: https://billzino.com/credit-note-guide.html)

**Q: Does every client need a purchase order?**

No. Small businesses often buy without one. Larger organisations usually require a PO before they can pay.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: What if the client has no PO number?**

Ask for one before you deliver. If they have none, note the approver's name and reference on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: Can I invoice without a PO?**

Yes, but expect delays with clients whose accounts payable team requires one.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: What is a 3-way match?**

Accounts payable matches the PO, the delivery note and the invoice before paying. That is why the numbers must match exactly.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: Does BillZino create purchase orders?**

You can title a document Purchase Order in the builder and list the items; the PDF layout is the same.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: What is a purchase order template?**

A purchase order template lists the buyer and supplier, a PO number, the date, the items with quantity and price, and delivery and payment terms. This guide shows the purchase order format line by line.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: What is the difference between a purchase order and an invoice?**

A purchase order is issued by the buyer before a sale to authorise the purchase; an invoice is issued by the seller after delivery to request payment. The PO number is usually repeated on the invoice.

(Source: https://billzino.com/purchase-order-guide.html)

**Q: How soon should I send a reminder?**

One to three days after the due date. Most late payments are administrative, not bad faith.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-email-templates.html)

**Q: Should I mention a late fee in the first email?**

No. Keep the first email friendly; introduce the fee in the second or third.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-email-templates.html)

**Q: Can I charge interest without a contract clause?**

In many countries yes, at the statutory rate; a written clause is always safer.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-email-templates.html)

**Q: What if the client disputes the invoice?**

Ask for the specific line in dispute and pause the late fee while you resolve it.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-email-templates.html)

**Q: When should I use a collection agency?**

After a final demand and a clear deadline have passed.

(Source: https://billzino.com/late-payment-email-templates.html)

## Free Receipt Maker & Generator – PDF in 60 Seconds
URL: https://billzino.com/receipt-generator.html
Summary: Free receipt maker and template: create a clean payment receipt online and download the PDF. No signup, no watermark. Add logo, items, tax and signature.

Proof of payment in under a minute. Fill in who paid, what for and how much, then download a print-ready PDF — no signup, no watermark.

### How to make a receipt in 3 steps

1. **Add the details** — Type your business name and address, the customer's name, the receipt number and the payment date.
2. **List what was paid for** — Add one line per item or service with quantity and price. Turn on tax, discount or shipping if they applied.
3. **Download the PDF** — Check the total, add your logo, signature or stamp if you want, then download an A4 PDF to send or keep.

### What is a receipt?

A receipt is a document that confirms a customer has paid. It records who paid, who received the money, what it was for, the amount and the date. Unlike an invoice, which asks for payment, a receipt shows that payment has already happened.

### What to include on a receipt

- **Your business name, address and contact details**
- **Receipt number** — a unique, sequential number (for example R-0001)
- **Date of payment**
- **Customer name** (and address if needed)
- **Itemised list** of goods or services with quantity and price
- **Subtotal, tax and total paid**
- **Payment method** — cash, bank transfer, card or other
- **Signature or stamp** (optional, but common for cash payments)

### Receipt vs invoice

|  | Invoice | Receipt |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Requests payment | Confirms payment was received |
| Sent | Before payment | After payment |
| Has a due date | Yes | Usually no |
| Shows amount | Amount due | Amount paid |

Need to ask for payment first? Use the [free invoice generator](https://billzino.com/index.html), then issue a receipt once the money arrives. See [invoice vs receipt vs quote](https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html) for the full comparison.

### Tips for better receipts

- Number every receipt in order and never reuse a number.
- Write the payment method so the record matches your bank or cash book.
- Keep a copy of every receipt — most tax authorities expect you to keep records for several years. Check your local rules.

**Q: Can I add tax to a receipt?**

Yes. Turn on the tax option, enter the percentage, and the total updates automatically.

**Q: What is the difference between a receipt and an invoice?**

An invoice asks a customer to pay. A receipt confirms the customer has already paid.

**Q: How do I create a receipt?**

Open the generator, enter who paid and who received the money, add the items and amount, choose the date and payment method, then download the receipt as a PDF. It works for a payment receipt or a simple sales receipt.

## Free Quote Generator – Price Quote PDF
URL: https://billzino.com/quote-generator.html
Summary: Free quote generator and template: create a professional price quote online and download a PDF. No signup, no watermark. Items, tax, logo and signature.

### How to make a quote in 3 steps

2. **Price every line** — Add each service or product with quantity and rate. Add a discount or tax if needed.
3. **Download and send** — Add your logo and signature, download the PDF and send it. When the client accepts, turn it into an invoice.

### What is a quote?

A quote (or quotation) is a document that tells a customer how much you will charge for a defined piece of work or set of products. It is an offer: once the customer accepts it, you deliver and then send an invoice.

### What to include in a quote

- **Your business details** and the client's details
- **Quote number and date**
- **Itemised scope** — each service or product with quantity and price
- **Total price**, including any tax, discount or shipping
- **Validity period** — for example “valid for 30 days”
- **Terms** — deposit, payment schedule, delivery time

### Quote vs estimate vs invoice

|  | Quote | Estimate | Invoice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | Fixed offer | Approximate | Final amount due |
| Binding | Usually yes, until it expires | No | Yes |
| Sent | Before work | Before work | After or at delivery |

After the client says yes, bill them with the [free invoice generator](https://billzino.com/index.html). For a deeper comparison read [invoice vs receipt vs quote](https://billzino.com/invoice-vs-receipt-vs-quote.html).

### Tips for quotes that get accepted

- Be specific about what is and isn't included to avoid scope arguments later.
- State how long the price is valid.
- Keep it to one page and send it quickly — fast replies win work.

**Q: How long should a quote be valid?**

Most quotes are valid for 14 to 30 days. Write the validity period on the quote so prices can change after it expires.

**Q: Can I add a discount or tax to a quote?**

Yes. Both are toggles in the builder and the total updates automatically.

**Q: What is the difference between a quote and an estimate?**

A quote is a fixed offer. An estimate is an approximate price that can change.

**Q: How do I create a quote?**

Open the generator, add your business and client details, list each item with a quantity and price, set a validity date and terms, then download the quote as a PDF. It works as a free quote template and quote maker: nothing to install, no signup.

**Q: Can I use this as a quotation template?**

Yes. Edit the line items, prices, tax and notes, and save the finished quotation as a PDF. Use a fresh quote each time, with its own number and validity date.

### What is a tax invoice?

A tax invoice is an invoice that shows the tax charged on a sale — such as VAT, GST or sales tax — as a separate amount. Many countries require businesses that charge tax to issue one so the buyer can reclaim it and the seller can report it.

### What to include on a tax invoice

- The words **“Tax Invoice”** on the document
- Your **business name, address and tax registration number** (if you have one)
- The customer's name and address
- A **unique invoice number** and the **date**
- A **description of each item**, quantity and price
- The **tax rate and tax amount**, shown separately
- The **total payableImportant:** tax invoice rules differ by country. BillZino gives you a clean layout and does the arithmetic, but it does not give tax advice — check what your tax authority requires.

### Tax invoice vs invoice

|  | Invoice | Tax invoice |
|---|---|---|
| Shows tax separately | Not necessarily | Yes |
| Tax registration number | Not required | Often required |
| Used when | No tax is charged | You charge VAT, GST or sales tax |

**Q: What format does a tax invoice follow?**

The usual tax invoice format shows seller and buyer details, a unique invoice number, the date, each line with quantity and price, the tax rate and amount, and the total. The generator lays these out for you; a sales tax invoice follows the same structure.

## Free Estimate Generator – Create a PDF
URL: https://billzino.com/estimate-generator.html
Summary: Free estimate generator: create a professional estimate online and download it as a PDF. No signup, no watermark. Scope, items and validity date.

Give the client an approximate price before the work — with scope, line items and a validity date.

### What an estimate is

**An estimate gives a client an approximate price before the work starts.** It is not a bill and it is not a fixed promise: it tells the client what the job is likely to cost, so they can decide whether to go ahead.

An estimate becomes useful when it is written down. A verbal number is forgotten; a PDF with a scope, a price range and a validity date is a document the client can approve.

### Estimate vs quote vs invoice

| Document | When | Binding? |
|---|---|---|
| Estimate | Before work, approximate | No — the final price can change |
| Quote | Before work, fixed price | Yes, usually for a stated period |
| Invoice | After or at delivery | Yes — it is a request for payment |

If you already know the exact price, send a [quote](https://billzino.com/quote-generator.html) instead. If the work is done, send an [invoice](https://billzino.com/index.html).

### What to include in an estimate

- The word **Estimate** at the top
- Estimate number and date
- Your details and the client's details
- A clear scope: what is included and what is not
- Line items with quantities and rates
- The estimated total, and whether tax is included
- How long the estimate is valid (for example 30 days)
- A note that the final price may change if the scope changes

### Example

| Item | Qty | Rate | Estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kitchen removal | 1 | 600.00 | 600.00 |
| Plumbing first fix | 16 h | 50.00 | 800.00 |
| Tiling (materials extra) | 22 m² | 35.00 | 770.00 |
| **Estimated total** |  |  | **2,170.00** |

Note the "materials extra" line: it tells the client the number is not final, which is exactly what an estimate is for.

### From estimate to invoice

When the job is done, create an invoice with the same line items, replace the estimated amounts with the real ones, and reference the estimate number. The client can compare the two documents without asking you to explain the difference.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the difference between an estimate and a quote?**

An estimate is approximate and can change; a quote is a fixed price, usually valid for a stated period.

**Q: Is an estimate legally binding?**

Usually no, unless your terms say otherwise. It is an indication of price, not a contract.

**Q: Should an estimate include tax?**

State clearly whether the amount includes tax. Many estimates show the total excluding tax and add a note.

**Q: How long should an estimate be valid?**

30 days is common. Put the validity date on the document so there is no ambiguity later.

**Q: Can I turn an estimate into an invoice?**

Yes. Reuse the same line items, update the amounts to the final figures, and reference the estimate number.

**Q: How do I create an estimate for a job?**

Open the generator, describe the work in line items with quantities and prices, add tax and notes, and download the estimate as a PDF. For a construction estimate, list labour and materials separately so the client can see what makes up the total.

**Q: Is there an estimate form I can fill in?**

Yes. The generator is a fillable estimate form: type in your details and items, and the totals update as you go.

## Free Proforma Invoice Generator – PDF in Minutes
URL: https://billzino.com/proforma-invoice-generator.html
Summary: Create a proforma invoice online and download the PDF. Free, no signup, no watermark. Includes what to show, how it differs from an invoice and an example.

Announce the exact amount before the sale is final — with the fields customs and finance teams expect.

### What a proforma invoice is

**A proforma invoice is an advance copy of an invoice, sent before the sale is final.** It tells the buyer exactly what they will be charged, so they can approve the purchase, arrange a transfer, or clear customs — but it is not a demand for payment and it is not a tax document.

The word "proforma" means "for the sake of form". Once the goods ship or the service is delivered, you replace it with a real invoice.

### When to use one

- **Prepayment:** the client needs a document before their finance team releases the money.
- **International shipping:** customs often ask for a proforma with the value and origin of the goods.
- **Budget approval:** a purchase order needs a price breakdown before it is issued.
- **Deposits:** you want to confirm the amount before the work starts.

### Proforma vs invoice

|  | Proforma invoice | Invoice |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Announce the price | Request payment |
| Accounting | Not recorded as revenue | Recorded as revenue |
| Tax | Usually no VAT/sales tax due | Tax charged and reported |
| When | Before delivery | At or after delivery |

### What to include

- The words **Proforma Invoice** and a number
- Issue date and, if relevant, an expiry date
- Seller and buyer details, including tax numbers
- Goods or services with quantity, unit price and total
- Currency, Incoterms and payment method for exports
- A clear note: "This is not a tax invoice"

### Example

| Description | Qty | Unit | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custom display stand | 2 | 450.00 | 900.00 |
| Shipping — DAP | 1 | 120.00 | 120.00 |
| **Proforma total** |  |  | **1,020.00** |

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is a proforma invoice a real invoice?**

No. It is an advance notice of the amount. The real invoice is issued after delivery and is the document used for accounting and tax.

**Q: Do I charge VAT on a proforma invoice?**

Usually no tax is due at the proforma stage. The real invoice carries the tax. Confirm with your accountant for cross-border cases.

**Q: Can a proforma invoice be used for customs?**

Yes, many customs authorities accept a proforma for valuation before shipment, but the commercial invoice is required for the final clearance.

**Q: What is the difference between a proforma and a quote?**

A quote offers a price before the client commits. A proforma confirms the exact amount for a sale that is already agreed.

**Q: Do I need to number proforma invoices?**

Yes, use a separate sequence such as PF-0001 so they are never confused with real invoices.

**Q: What is a proforma invoice?**

A proforma invoice is a preliminary document that lists what you will sell, the quantities and the prices before the sale is final. It is not a request for payment in the accounting sense, and it does not replace the final invoice. Some countries also call it a pro forma invoice.

**Q: What is the difference between a proforma invoice and a commercial invoice?**

A proforma invoice is issued before shipment as an estimate of the sale; a commercial invoice is issued after the sale and is the final record used for payment and customs. BillZino does not generate customs documents.
